title: Account Takeover via Shared Invitation Token
summary:
### Summary

A batch invitation issued one shared invite token to every recipient, so any one invitee could complete another invitee's signup and take control of that pending account.

### Details

The organisation, base and workspace invite paths - `org-users.service.ts`, `base-users.service.ts` and `workspace-users.service.ts`, with the enterprise overrides of the latter two carrying the same shape independently - generated a single token value outside the per-recipient loop and stored it on every user row the operation created. Signup acceptance in `users.service.ts` looked the pending user up by the submitted email address and then compared the submitted token against that row's own token, so a token shared across the batch validated for every address in it; the holder could set the password on an account that was never theirs. A defective expiry check compounded this: the invite token's expiry was compared as a stored string against a `Date`, a comparison that never evaluated true, so tokens did not age out.

### Impact

A user who received one invitation could take over the pending account of any other user invited in the same operation, including an account invited at a higher role, by completing that signup and choosing its password. Exploitation requires holding a valid invitation issued in the same batch as the target.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@aisle-research](https://github.com/aisle-research) (AISLE).
